newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir cosmonauts packing up to return home.
newsitem.headline: Mir cosmonauts packing up to return home.

text.p: Cosmonauts aboard the damaged space station Mir are cleaning up the ship and preparing to return home in two weeks after the most troubled mission in the space station's 11-year history, officials said on Tuesday.

"They are preparing for the arrival of the new crew, which means a series of both medical and physical exercises," spokeswoman Vera Medvedkova said from Russian Mission Control outside Moscow. "The new crew expects to launch on August 5 and connect with Mir on August 7."

The Mir, a collection of diverse modules arrayed around a core station, collided with its resupply ship on June 25, damaging its solar energy system and forcing the crew to seal off the Spektr module where scientific experiments were performed.

Space officials decided to delay repairing the Spektr after commander Vasily Tsibliyev, 43, developed heart trouble and then the crew plunged into another crisis by accidently unplugging a vital computer, causing the station to lose its orientation for Doctors at Mission Control on July 15 prescribed sedatives and medicine to stabilise Tsibliyev's heart beat, and his condition has improved in recent days, Medvedkova said.
"His heart medicine has been discontinued and they are giving him pharmecological support with vitamins and sedatives, because his cardiogram shows that everything is fine," she said.
Tsibliyev on Sunday celebrated a year of cumulative time in space, including his present mission and one in 1993-94.

Among the chores facing the crew is loading old food containers and other garbage aboard the Progress ship Tsibliyev and flight engineer Alexander Lazutkin will use it to return to earth on August 14, NASA spokeswoman Kathleen Maliga said.
They are also using a CO2 scrubber they repaired over the weekend to remove carbon dioxide from the air, she said.
British-born NASA physicist Michael Foale, who has continued work on several scientific experiments in recent days, will stay on board until a U.S. shuttle arrives on September 20.
NASA astronaut Wendy Lawrence, a U.S. Navy commander, is scheduled to replace the British-born Foale.

The Russian crew, which came aboard on February 12, is also paving the way for their replacements to make repairs soon after their arrival by moving around equipment and performing other tasks, officials said.
The new crew of commander Anatoly Solovyov and flight engineer Pavel Vinogradov plan to reconnect the solar panel cables inside the 12-metre- (yard) long Spektr between August 18 and 20.
Then in early September they are expected to make a space walk to inspect the external puncture in the Spektr which has forced them to seal it off from the rest of the ship.
Over the weekend the Mir crew repaired one of four non-working gyrodynes which help the space station maintain its orientation toward the sun so its solar panels continue to gather energy.
They also talked to their families, space officials said.
At a news conference, Russian Space Agency chief Yuri Koptev on Tuesday repeated his estimate that repairing the damage will cost the equivalent of $15 million to $20 million.
